# Independent audit: tetrahedral cap variance and actual section-centroid products

Source audited: `candidate fa0b1651cc72d020`.

Result: PASS for the stated ordinary tetrahedral theorem and its scoped common-centroid corollary. No correction to the proof is needed.

I independently compared the four section-centroid formulas with the normalized reciprocal-diagonal formulas, retaining unequal and repeated positive/negative heights. The two cap-fraction expressions agree after their removable p=q denominator is canceled; the displayed final denominator remains strictly positive for every strict quadrilateral.

The independent checker `supporting computation verify_cap_variance_audit_two_sided.py` parses ALL 33 coefficient rows from the actual Markdown source (rather than copying the coefficient table into its code), reconstructs the 100-monomial polynomial, verifies positivity of every coefficient, and verifies the complete rational identity. Thus the proof covers the whole positive four-height domain and all equal-height cases, not merely a finite set of samples.

For triangular cuts, the reduction is exactly

    eta_j(1-product eta_i) <= sum_i(1-eta_i),

after division by the positive vertex-cap fraction and the positive intercept eta_j. Both factors used to prove it have the correct direction. Reversing the cap is harmless because F(1-F) is unchanged. Proper through-edge and through-vertex sections retain positive section area; the transverse-coordinate dominated-convergence argument for section areas and first moments is valid. Boundary planes have zero tetrahedral volume.

The stated sharpness is attained at the genuine proper section with intercepts (z,1,1), 0<z<1. Its section centroid is ((1-z)/3,z/3,1/3,1/3); omitting either of the last two coordinates gives complementary product z(1-z)/27. Thus a smaller universal coefficient cannot replace 27.

For the common-centroid corollary, minimizing the complementary triple product indeed means excluding a largest centroid coordinate. In the unique-noncentral setting this is the distinguished h coordinate. The separate strict captured-vertex product theorem supplies F>C(b) for each h-oriented quadrilateral; the new theorem gives F(1-F)<C(b). Neither inequality by itself is promoted to the still-unproved three-cap probability support comparison. All constants and strictness statements in this scope are correct.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
